clue.text: Went astray, shortly going round town in County Clare

indicators.note: turning round means the letters left are read backwards
cut short, so the last letter of the word for going astray is dropped

parts.note: to go astray morally is to sin, so went astray is sinned

explanation.surface: Someone wandered off and got lost, circling a town in the west of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' trims SINNED to SINNE, and 'going round' turns that into the town's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennis is the county town of Clare in the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Fantastic support arose for what Brexiters will now deny us

definitions.text: what Brexiters will now deny us

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: Strong backing grew for something the Leave campaign takes from Britons.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving the EU ended British citizens' entitlement to the burgundy EU travel document.

clue.text: Rate no sin bad, being a heretic

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: Calling no sin bad is the mark of an unorthodox believer.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Nestorius, whose teaching on Christ's nature was condemned as heresy in 431.

clue.text: Smart singer

definitions.meaning: to smart is to hurt with a sharp pain
the stage name of the lead singer of The Police

explanation.definitionFit: A sting smarts; Gordon Sumner performs as Sting.

clue.text: Report of Conservative party leader no longer thriving

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the letters are said aloud and taken by their sound

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives; Ming was the nickname of Sir Menzies Campbell, a former Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: News about a Tory leader who has lost the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative' gives BLUE, and 'party leader no longer' is Ming Campbell, who led the Liberal Democrats until 2007; said together they make the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that is flourishing is in full flower, so thriving is a synonym.

clue.text: Street poet outside old university getting money from Bulgaria

indicators.note: the poet word goes outside the other pieces

parts.note: a bard is a poet
the lev is the Bulgarian currency

explanation.surface: A street poet from an old university receives Bulgarian cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulevard is a broad, often tree-lined city avenue.

clue.text: Nothing was gripping in newspaper notice

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
bit, the past of bite, means was gripping with the teeth

explanation.surface: A newspaper notice that held no interest at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for obituary, the press notice of a person's death.

clue.text: Tramp? Patch up one with affected piety

parts.note: to mend is to patch up
I is the Roman numeral for one
cant is hypocritically pious talk

explanation.surface: A vagrant mends his clothes while putting on holy airs.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant lives by begging, so a tramp is one example.

clue.text: Child of immigrant couple that is beginning to settle in after upheaval?

indicators.note: in a down clue an upheaval lifts the letters up, reading them bottom to top

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A couple's child born after they have uprooted to settle abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'after upheaval' means the pieces are read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese term for an American or Canadian born to parents who emigrated from Japan.

clue.text: Backward-looking philosophy to suit minister being nasty

indicators.note: behaving nastily suggests the words are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A reactionary creed that suits a spiteful government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctrine favours restoring past conditions, hence a philosophy looking backwards.

clue.text: Maybe Thor's not given enough bangs for his bucks?

definitions.text: not given enough bangs for his bucks?

parts.note: the word short, its letters changed, gives Thor's

explanation.surface: The thunder god feels cheated of value for money.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, an anagram of SHORT, gives the clue's THOR'S. 'Bangs for his bucks' plays on Thor's thunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheated out of money owed, or getting poor value, is to be given too little.

clue.text: Failed to be ready for new phase of agriculture?

definitions.meaning: old British student slang: to fail an examination

definitions.text: ready for new phase of agriculture?
definitions.meaning: a field turned over by the plough is prepared for sowing, the next stage of farming

explanation.surface: A farmer flops just as a new season of farming begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploughed land is prepared for sowing; the exam sense of failing is dated British slang.

clue.text: Complete home: perhaps dab on the outside

indicators.note: the flatfish word sits around the outside of the word for home

parts.note: a dab is a kind of flatfish, so 'perhaps' marks it as an example of fish
in means at home

explanation.surface: Finishing a house by dabbing paint on its exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dab' looks like a painting action, but it is a flatfish, and 'on the outside' puts it around the word for home.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete a job is to bring it to an end, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Unjustifiably claimed an idiot's wrong — answers finally will get stuck in

indicators.note: the final letter is pushed into the middle of the rearranged letters
something wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boast is unfounded: a fool's answers are wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of AN IDIOTS ('wrong') has the S from the end of 'answers' put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan phrase means self-styled, describing a status asserted without real warrant.

clue.text: Suffer with a bitter feeling, not one that will afflict you for ever

definitions.text: that will afflict you for ever

parts.note: to incur a loss is to suffer it

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: bile is bitterness or anger
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Suffering bitterness can be a lifelong condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease that cannot be cured stays with the patient permanently.

clue.text: Note a Guardian columnist, one boiling up inside?

parts.note: te is the seventh note of the tonic sol-fa scale
Martin Kettle is a long-standing Guardian columnist

explanation.surface: A Guardian columnist seething with suppressed anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Water heats inside the pot on a stove, a playful description of the vessel.

clue.text: Like that woman Jane who went out with Paul?

definitions.text: Jane who went out with Paul?

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Asking who resembles the woman who dated Paul.
explanation.walkthrough: The actress Jane Asher was Paul McCartney's girlfriend in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the actress famously engaged to the Beatle in the sixties.

clue.text: What Scot does in street — refuses to budge

definitions.meaning: the word Scot is ST, the short form of street, holding CO, the short form of company or firm
stays put and will not give way

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a reverse reading: take the answer as an instruction, ST holding CO, and you build the clue's SCOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay resolute and not give way is to stand fast, an idiom for refusing to yield.

clue.text: International organisation in illustration of old city

indicators.note: the organisation's letters go inside the word for illustration

parts.note: a pic is a short form of picture, an illustration
UN stands for the United Nations

explanation.surface: The UN shown in a picture of some ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to Carthage, the ancient North African city, as in the Punic Wars.

clue.text: Little woman's surprisingly stoical — that blood pressure's at the lower end

definitions.text: blood pressure's at the lower end

parts.note: Di is a short form of the woman's name Diana; the 's joins it on

indicators.note: a surprising turn signals the next word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small woman stays remarkably calm while her blood pressure is low.
explanation.definitionFit: The diastolic figure is the lower number of a blood-pressure reading, taken between heartbeats.

clue.text: Engineers left account of progress made?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Army engineers walked off and left a progress account behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a written account, such as a school report on a pupil's progress.

clue.text: Something needed for 1 down recently taken in post office?

indicators.note: one word sits inside the other

parts.note: hot goods are recently stolen

explanation.surface: A picture needed for a travel document, snapped at the post office.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel documents carry a picture of the holder, so one is needed to apply.

clue.text: Possibly the bed's a place of healing

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Maybe a bed is the best spot to recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is the pool in Jerusalem where, in John's gospel, Jesus healed a lame man.

clue.text: Leave house and topple over

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to tip over is to topple

explanation.surface: Get out of the house before it falls down.
explanation.definitionFit: A brusque British idiom telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Rex and Brian in a gambling centre

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king
Brian Eno is the musician and producer

explanation.surface: A king and a man named Brian at a casino town.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno in Nevada is famous for its casinos, a city of betting.

clue.text: Ringers with excellent musical technique

parts.note: dead ringers are exact lookalikes, doubles
topping is old British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Bell-ringers with superb musical skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringers' suggests bell-ringing; here it means lookalikes, as in 'dead ringers'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a violin or cello, playing two strings at once is a recognised technique of the bow.

clue.text: Killer of insects — one by mechanical process getting any number

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: rote is mechanical repetition, as in learning by rote
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: An insecticide that works mechanically on any number of bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotenone is a plant-derived pesticide used against insects and fish.

clue.text: Bit about your setter being like a pussycat?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The puzzle-setter has a bit of a gentle, kittenish side.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamed animal is docile and gentle, as a pet cat typically is.
